explanation: Compare the first and last characters and move inward. Every mirrored pair must match exactly; case and punctuation remain significant.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. At most floor(n/2) mirrored pairs are compared.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Only two indices or a constant-space generator are retained.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: A string equals its reversal exactly when every pair of positions equidistant from the two ends contains the same character. The two-pointer loop checks all such pairs and rejects at the first mismatch.
walkthrough: For "q7x7q", compare q with q, then 7 with 7. The middle x has no partner to check, so return true.
edgeCases: Empty and one-character strings are palindromes.
Case and punctuation remain significant in this exact-comparison problem.
An odd middle character does not affect the result.
Character positions in this implementation are UTF-16 code units, not user-perceived grapheme clusters.
